ambiguities.description: Customer naming convention: Can a customer have multiple names, or is the name field single-valued? The transcript states 'every customer has a name' but does not clarify whether a single customer can have multiple names (e.g., legal name vs. display name) or whether each customer is restricted to exactly one name.

ambiguities.description: Customer vs. Client definition: The Product Manager indicates that 'customers' in CRM and 'clients' in the billing system are the same concept but with a key difference -- the billing team only considers someone a client after they've paid. Should Customer and Client be modeled as separate entity types with distinct identification schemes, or is this purely a process/workflow distinction that doesn't affect the data model? Does the model need to track payment status to distinguish between unpaid customers and paid clients?

source_references.excerpt: I've heard some people call customers "clients" in the billing system. Are those the same thing? ... Good question. In our CRM they're "customers" but the billing team calls them "clients." For our purposes they're the same concept but the billing team has a slightly different definition -- they only consider someone a client once they've actually paid.
